title.zh: 卷一百十三 列傳第六十三: 苗晉卿 裴冕 裴遵慶
title.en: Volume 113 Biographies 63: Miao Jingqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing
title.raw: 卷一百十三 列傳第六十三: 苗晉卿 裴冕 裴遵慶 Volume 113 Biographies 63: Miao Jingqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞

translations.literal: Miao Jingqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, Zi Xiang, Zi Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jingqing; Pei Mian; Pei Zunqing; Zi Xiang; Zi Xiang's son Yin; Yin's son Shu.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。

translations.literal: Miao Jingqing was a man of Huguan in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jingqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: For generations the family was famed for Confucian integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been known for scholarly rectitude and plain living.

sentences.zh: 祖夔，高道不仕，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui was a man of lofty character who did not take office; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui was a man of exalted principle who never entered government service; he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His father Daiyi reached the post of Assistant Magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture, died young, and through Jingqing was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daiyi had served as assistant magistrate of Longmen county in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jingqing's honors he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Jingqing from youth loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jingqing was devoted to study and gifted at writing; he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Magistrate of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, served as Magistrate of Fengxian, and through accumulated offenses was demoted to Registrar of Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed magistrate of Xiuwu county in Huai prefecture, later served as magistrate of Fengxian, and was eventually demoted to registrar of Xu prefecture after a series of entanglements.

sentences.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。

translations.literal: When his term expired he followed the regular transfer, was judged in the upper grade, and was appointed Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he entered the regular reassignment process, received a top evaluation, and was appointed magistrate of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of attending censor and then served in turn as vice director in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 (735) he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he and Sun Di, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, were together appointed Drafting Attendants at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he and Sun Di of the Ministry of Personnel were jointly appointed drafting attendants at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, in his existing post he was temporarily charged with managing personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 27 (739) he was given temporary charge of civil-service selection while retaining his secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。

translations.literal: Jingqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates brought lawsuits or demanded good posts, even if they spoke thousands of words or their voices and expressions were very fierce, Jingqing always bore with them and showed not the least anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing was by nature modest and mild-mannered. When candidates came with petitions or demands for favorable appointments—even haranguing him at length or raising their voices in anger—he always received them patiently and never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 (741) he was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。

translations.literal: Over five years in charge of selection, administration grew lax, clerks widely used opportunities for villainy, and bribery flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw selection for five years in all. Because his administration was lenient, clerks found countless openings for abuse and bribery became rampant.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。

translations.literal: At the time the realm enjoyed peace; each year more than ten thousand commonly came for selection.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace, and each year more than ten thousand candidates typically presented themselves for examination.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu was Minister and monopolized court affairs; selection matters were entrusted solely to Jingqing and his fellow Vice Minister Song Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, as minister of personnel, kept his grip on court power and left the business of selection entirely to Jingqing and his colleague Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。

translations.literal: Because candidates were numerous, each year other officials of discernment were also ordered to examine and grade written judgments jointly, striving for truth.
translations.idiomatic: With so many candidates, each year other knowledgeable officials were also assigned to grade the written examinations together, so that the results might be as fair as possible.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Zhang Yi's son Shi entered selection; Jingqing and Yao, because Yi had newly received favor, wished to please and attach themselves to him; they graded sixty-four candidates in written judgment into jia, yi, and bing classes, with Shi at the head.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi sat for the examinations. Jingqing and Yao, wishing to curry favor with Yi, who had only recently risen in the emperor's grace, ranked sixty-four candidates in three grades—and placed Shi at the top.

sentences.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。

translations.literal: The multitude knew Shi did not read books, and debate arose in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew that Shi was barely literate, and public outcry spread.

sentences.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。

translations.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin who had once been Magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and reported the whole affair to him in detail.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Su Xiaoyin, who had once been magistrate of Ji in Fanyang and was now in An Lushan's service, reported the whole affair to him in detail.

sentences.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。

translations.literal: Lushan enjoyed exceptional favor and was not often received in audience; he therefore memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan enjoyed extraordinary favor at court and was not often granted audience; he seized the occasion to present a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；

translations.literal: Xuanzong greatly assembled those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Tower, and of those who had passed, not one or two in ten [succeeded];
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned all the newly passed candidates to the Hua'e Tower for a personal examination; fewer than one in ten proved able to pass;

sentences.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: but Shi held the examination paper and for a whole day did not write a single character; at the time they called it 'dragging the blank.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi, holding his examination paper, could not write a single character all day long—people at the time called it 'dragging a blank sheet.'

sentences.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Jingqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang commandery, and Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Jingqing was demoted to prefect of Ankang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Zhang Yi to prefect of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Within one's own gate and courtyard, one cannot instruct one's son;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'At home he could not teach his son;

sentences.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。」

translations.literal: at the time of selection and transfer, he still relied on entrusting others.
translations.idiomatic: at selection time he still had to rely on pulling strings for others.

sentences.zh: 時士子皆以為戲笑。

translations.literal: At the time scholars all took it as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere treated the edict as a public joke.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載閏二月，轉魏郡太守，充河北采訪處置使，居職三年，政化洽聞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the third year of Tianbao he was transferred to Prefect of Wei commandery and served as Hebei Investigation and Disposition Commissioner; in three years in office his civilizing influence was widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of Tianbao 3 (744) he was made prefect of Wei and commissioner for investigation and disposition in Hebei. After three years in office his good governance was renowned throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 會入計，因上表請歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When he came in for the annual accounting he therefore submitted a memorial requesting to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled to the capital for the annual review of accounts, he submitted a memorial asking leave to visit his home.

sentences.zh: 既至壺關，望縣門而步。

translations.literal: When he reached Huguan he saw the county gate and walked [on foot].
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huguan he dismounted and walked as he approached the county gate.

sentences.zh: 小吏進曰：「太守位高德重，不宜自輕。」

translations.literal: A petty clerk advanced and said: 'The prefect's position is high and his virtue weighty; he should not slight himself.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk stepped forward and said, 'Your Excellency's rank and standing are too high—you should not humble yourself in this way.

sentences.zh: 晉卿曰：「《禮》：『下公門，式路馬。』

translations.literal: Jingqing said: 'The Rites states: "When descending from the duke's gate, one salutes the road horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing replied, 'The Book of Rites says: When one leaves a lord's gate, one bows toward the horses on the road.

sentences.zh: 況父母之邦，所宜尊敬。

translations.literal: How much more is one's parents' homeland what ought to be respected.
translations.idiomatic: How much more should one show respect in the land of one's parents?

sentences.zh: 汝何言哉！」

translations.literal: What words are these of yours!"
translations.idiomatic: What sort of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 大會鄉黨，歡飲累日而去。

translations.literal: He held a great gathering of fellow townsmen, feasted joyfully for many days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He gave a great feast for his kinsmen and neighbors, celebrated for several days, and then took his leave.

sentences.zh: 又俸錢三萬為鄉學本，以教授子弟。

translations.literal: He also set aside thirty thousand in salary cash as capital for a district school to instruct the young.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted thirty thousand cash from his salary as an endowment for a village school to educate local youths.

sentences.zh: 尋改河東太守、河東采訪使，入為尚書、東京留守，征為憲部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prefect of Hedong and Hedong Investigation Commissioner, entered the capital as Minister and Eastern Capital Regent, and was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Hedong and commissioner for investigation there, then recalled to serve as a minister and regent of the eastern capital, and finally summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山叛逆，楊國忠以晉卿有時望，將抑之，乃奏云：「宜以大臣鎮東道。」

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, because Jingqing enjoyed contemporary esteem and wished to suppress him, memorialized saying: 'A great minister ought to guard the eastern circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Yang Guozhong—wishing to sideline Jingqing, who still commanded wide respect—memorialized that a senior minister should be posted to guard the eastern circuit.

sentences.zh: 遂出為陜州刺史、陜虢兩州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as Prefect of Shan prefecture and Defense Commissioner of the two prefectures of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing was accordingly sent out as prefect of Shan and defense commissioner for Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 及入對，固辭老病，由是忤旨，改憲部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When he entered for audience he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness; thereby he offended the imperial will and was changed to Minister of Justice with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared at court he firmly pleaded age and illness. The emperor took offense, and Jingqing was made minister of justice in name only and retired from active duty.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷失守，衣冠流離道路，多為逆黨所脅，自陳希烈、張均已下數十人盡赴洛陽，晉卿潛遁山谷，南投金州。

translations.literal: When the court lost the capital, officials in caps and gowns wandered the roads, many compelled by the rebel faction; from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun downward dozens all went to Luoyang, while Jingqing secretly fled into mountain valleys and went south to Jin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, officials fled in every direction, many forced into the rebels' service. Dozens of men from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun on down made their way to Luoyang, but Jingqing slipped into the hills and fled south to Jin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗至鳳翔，手詔追晉卿赴行在，即日拜為左相，軍國大務悉以咨之。

translations.literal: When Suzong reached Fengxiang, by handwritten edict he summoned Jingqing to the mobile court; that same day he was appointed Left Counselor, and all great affairs of army and state were entirely referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, he sent a personal edict summoning Jingqing to the temporary court. That very day Jingqing was made left counselor, and all major military and civil affairs were entrusted to his counsel.

sentences.zh: 既收兩京，以功封韓國公，食實封五百戶，改為侍中。

translations.literal: After recovering the two capitals, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han with five hundred actual households, and was changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were retaken, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han with an income of five hundred households and appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以賊寇漸除，屢乞骸骨，優詔許之，罷知政事，為太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later, as bandits were gradually eliminated, he repeatedly begged to surrender his bones; by gracious edict this was granted, he ceased managing state affairs, and became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels were gradually subdued he repeatedly asked to retire. The emperor graciously consented, relieved him of administrative duties, and made him grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝思舊臣，復拜為侍中。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor thought of old ministers and again appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor, missing his veteran ministers, appointed him palace attendant once more.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚廉謹，為政舉大綱，不問小過，所到有惠化。

translations.literal: Jingqing was generous, honest, and cautious; in government he upheld great principles, did not inquire into small faults, and wherever he went there was benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing was magnanimous, upright, and careful in office. He governed by broad principles rather than petty fault-finding, and everywhere he served left a record of humane rule.

sentences.zh: 魏人思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Wei remembered him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei cherished his memory and erected a monument in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及秉鈞衡，小心畏慎，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: When he held the balance of power he was careful and cautious and never once went against people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: When he held the highest offices he was cautious and deferential and never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，達練事體，百司文簿，經目必曉，而修身守位，以智自全，議者比漢之胡廣。

translations.literal: His nature was intelligent and keen; he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs; documents of the hundred offices, once seen, he always understood; yet in cultivating himself and keeping his position he preserved himself by wisdom—commentators compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and thoroughly understood how government worked; a glance at any document from any ministry was enough for him to grasp it. Yet he cultivated himself and kept his post by prudence, preserving himself through tact—critics compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 玄宗崩，肅宗詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jingqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong died, Emperor Suzong ordered Jingqing to serve as regent during the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞古者殷高宗在諒闇之中，百官聽於冢宰，更無事跡，但存文字。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: 'Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin was in the dark of mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent—there are no further traces of events, only written records remain.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a firm refusal, writing: 'I have read that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of the Yin was in mourning seclusion, the hundred officials took their orders from the regent—but beyond that tradition we have only written records, not living precedent.

sentences.zh: 且一時之事，禮不相沿。

translations.literal: Moreover, affairs of one time are not carried on by ritual from another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, rites suited to one age are not simply carried forward into another.

sentences.zh: 今殘寇猶虞，日殷萬務，皆緣兵馬屯守討襲，善算良謀，立勝擒敵。

translations.literal: Now remnant bandits still give concern; daily the myriad affairs press urgently—all depend on armies garrisoned, stationed, attacking, and raiding, on good calculation and fine strategy to achieve swift victory and capture the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Today remnant rebels still threaten the realm, and ten thousand urgent matters press upon us daily—all depending on armies in the field, on sound planning and bold strategy to win swift victories and capture the enemy.

sentences.zh: 陛下若行古之道，居喪不言，蒼生何依，百事皆廢。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way, dwells in mourning and does not speak, on what will the common people rely? A hundred affairs will all be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty were to follow the ancient way, remain in mourning, and hold your tongue, what would become of the people? Every affair of state would come to a halt.

sentences.zh: 伏讀國家起居註，亦於禮部檢見舊敕，恭惟太宗、高宗、、大行皇帝在位之日，皆有國哀，視事不輟，以為君臨天下，難徇常情。

translations.literal: Your servant has respectfully read the court diaries of the state and also in the Ministry of Rites examined old edicts; respectfully considering that during the days when Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and the late emperor held the throne, there were all national mourning periods yet they did not cease conducting affairs, taking it that to rule all under Heaven one cannot indulge ordinary feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully read the court diaries and found old edicts in the Ministry of Rites showing that Emperors Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and the late emperor, even during periods of national mourning, never ceased to conduct state business—for one who rules the realm, ordinary private feeling cannot be indulged.

sentences.zh: 今遺詔有處分，皇帝宜三日而聽政。

translations.literal: Now the testamentary edict has provisions: the emperor ought on the third day to hear government.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's testamentary edict expressly provides that the new emperor should assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 陛下遵太宗故事，則無冢宰；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, then there is no regent;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows Emperor Taizong's precedent, no regent is needed;

sentences.zh: 遵大行皇帝遺詔，便合聽朝。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testamentary edict, then it is fitting to hear court.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testamentary edict, you should take the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 萬姓颙颙，不勝大願。

translations.literal: The myriad people look up in eager longing—they cannot bear their great wish [unfulfilled].
translations.idiomatic: The people look to you with eager hope—they can scarcely contain their longing.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下知理國之重，順人心之切，以義斷恩，從宜無改。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that Your Majesty knows the weight of ordering the state, follows the urgency of people's hearts, breaks affection by righteousness, and should follow what is fitting without change.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to recognize how heavy is the burden of governing the realm, how urgent the people's need, and to let duty override private grief—to do what the occasion requires and not waver.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣一命已上，皆言臣心昏貌朽，加以疾病，事有急速，斷在須臾，凡聖不同，豈合受詔。

translations.literal: Today court ministers of the first rank and above all say your servant's mind is dim and his appearance decayed; added to this are illness; affairs of urgency must be decided in an instant; ordinary and sage are not the same—how is it fitting to receive the edict?
translations.idiomatic: Today every minister of the highest rank declares that my mind is clouded, my body worn out, and my illnesses many; urgent affairs must be decided in a moment—how can an ordinary man be equal to a sage? I am not fit to receive such an appointment.

sentences.zh: 陛下發哀已五日矣，願準遺詔聽政，則四夷萬國，無任悲幸。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has begun mourning for five days already; I wish you would follow the testamentary edict and hear government—then the four barbarians and ten thousand states will be without limit in grief and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already mourned for five days. I pray that you will follow the testamentary edict and take up governance—then the four quarters and all nations will know both grief and boundless relief.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時疾彌留，覽表殞絕，乃許。

translations.literal: Suzong's illness at the time was lingering near death; reading the memorial he collapsed as if dead, then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was then gravely ill. When he read the memorial he was overcome with emotion, but he granted the request.

sentences.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: Several days later Suzong died; Daizong ascended the throne and again ordered Jingqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Emperor Suzong died. When Emperor Daizong took the throne he again ordered Jingqing to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。

translations.literal: Jingqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: 'Your servant considers that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent—this was because the ruler was young and small, and assuming the apex while affairs were pressing was in reason and feeling naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing submitted another earnest refusal, writing: 'In former ages, when the Son of Heaven was in mourning, the hundred officials took orders from a regent only because the ruler was a child and the burdens of rule were too heavy for him—circumstance made it necessary.

sentences.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Continuity and change are not uniform; present and past differ and agree; yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han conformed to adapting through change, handed down models and made standards that can be raised up and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Customs have changed from age to age, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted rites to circumstance and left models we may follow today.

sentences.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。

translations.literal: Moreover, a gentleman may wear ink mourning garb yet encounter weapons and armor—this is not contrary to holding grief; it means righteousness lies in breaking affection.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a gentleman in deep mourning may still take up arms when the state is at war—he does not cease to grieve, but duty requires him to set private feeling aside.

sentences.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。

translations.literal: Moreover, of the hundred virtues none surpasses filial piety; yet there are those whose appearance is haggard and whose heart is severed, who point to the sun and mourn life—this is the ordinary feeling of a common man keeping integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king continuing the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet the common man who wastes away in grief, who can scarcely bear to live—such feeling belongs to private life, not to the great business of a king who must continue the dynastic line.

sentences.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。

translations.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty at the bier of the late emperor assumed the throne—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging institution of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Only twenty days ago Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's coffin—fulfilling his final charge and following an immemorial precedent.

sentences.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that what is set aside is not harmful, what is preserved is fitting expedience, guarding against peril and extinguishing beginnings—the benefit is great.
translations.idiomatic: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved serves the greater good. To guard against danger at its root brings the greatest benefit.

sentences.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart arising in purity reaches utmost sincerity; Heaven and Earth clearly perceive.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial heart is utterly sincere—Heaven and Earth themselves bear witness.

sentences.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！

translations.literal: Your servant considers that repaying the grace of toil and hardship, expressing boundless longing, a lifetime's pain—how could it be reckoned by days and nights!
translations.idiomatic: To repay a parent's labor, to express boundless grief—such sorrow lasts a lifetime and cannot be measured by days alone.

sentences.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。

translations.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs lie at the center; the imperial ear must be reached before state government can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs demand the throne's attention; only when Your Majesty's ear is open to them can the state be governed.

sentences.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, monks and Daoists, elders of long years, and others look at one another and gather in speech, saying your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity fathom sageliness? Moreover, for long there has been no regency; your servant dares not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, common people, monks, Daoist priests, and elders alike declare that I am old and incompetent, far too dull to measure up to a sage ruler—and besides, regency has long been out of use. I dare not accept this appointment.

sentences.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。

translations.literal: I especially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。」

translations.literal: Your servant broadly hears the multitude's feelings and cannot bear the earnest wish; I respectfully hope you will cut pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will grieve and rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard the people's voice throughout the realm, I cannot contain my earnest plea: I beg Your Majesty to master your grief for the sake of the empire—then the world will know both sorrow and deliverance.

sentences.zh: 上號泣從之。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and assented.

sentences.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。

translations.literal: At the time Jingqing's years were already declining into old age and he also suffered in both feet; the emperor specially permitted him to be carried in a shoulder litter to the Secretariat, to enter the gate without hastening, and to review affairs once every several days.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jingqing was elderly and afflicted in both legs. The emperor specially allowed him to be carried in a sedan chair to the Secretariat, to enter the hall without hurrying, and to conduct business only every few days.

sentences.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。

translations.literal: Through three reigns he was all praised for cautious discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Through three reigns he was esteemed for his caution and discretion.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era the Tibetans attacked Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。

translations.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak, and the bandits did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1 (765).

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court was suspended three days; one Junior Administrator of the Capital was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items connected with burial were supplied by the state; condolence gifts were five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days; a junior capital official was assigned to oversee the funeral; all burial expenses were paid by the state, with five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and gave the posthumous title "Yi-xian."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Yi-xian ("Reverent and Dedicated").

sentences.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Eastern Capital Retention Officer, he brought in Yuan Zai, Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jinqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Minister; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous title to Wen-zhen.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Zai was vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister; remembering old kindness, he prompted the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen-zhen ("Cultured and Upright").

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 7 (772) he was ordered to share sacrifices in Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 裴冕，河東人也，為河東冠族。

translations.literal: Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and was a leading clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian was a native of Hedong and belonged to one of the region's foremost families.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以門廕再遷渭南縣尉，以吏道聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice promoted to Magistrate of Weinan and became known for the way of clerical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he entered office through hereditary privilege and was twice promoted to magistrate of Weinan, where he won a reputation for administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王鉷充京畿采訪使，表為判官。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong served as Metropolitan Investigation Commissioner and recommended him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, vice censor-in-chief and metropolitan investigation commissioner, recommended him as an administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor and successively served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to investigating censor and then served as attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 冕雖無學術，守職通明，果於臨事，鉷甚委之。

translations.literal: Although Mian had no scholarly learning, in keeping office he was clear and penetrating, decisive in facing affairs, and Hong greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mian had little formal learning, he was clear-minded and capable in office and decisive when action was required; Wang Hong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪伏法，時宰臣李林甫方竊權柄，人鹹懼之，鉷賓佐數百，不敢窺鉷門。

translations.literal: When Hong was guilty and executed by law, at the time Chief Minister Li Linfu was just stealing the handles of power and people all feared him; Hong's guests and aides numbered in the hundreds and dared not peer at Hong's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong was condemned and executed, Chief Minister Li Linfu held unchecked power and everyone lived in fear. Hundreds of men who had served under Hong did not dare even approach his house.

sentences.zh: 冕獨收鉷屍，親自護喪，瘞於近郊，冕自是知名。

translations.literal: Mian alone recovered Hong's corpse, personally escorted the mourning, and buried him in the near suburbs; from this Mian became known.
translations.idiomatic: Mian alone recovered Hong's body, personally conducted the funeral, and buried him in a suburban grave—and from that day his name was known.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰表為行軍司馬，累遷員外郎中。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, Military Commissioner of Hexi, recommended him as campaigning marshal and he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, appointed him campaigning marshal, and he rose through several posts to vice director.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，至益昌郡，遙詔太子充天下兵馬元帥，以冕為御史中丞兼左庶子，為之副。

translations.literal: Xuanzong went to Shu; when he reached Yichang commandery, by distant edict the Heir Apparent was made Commander-in-Chief of all armies under Heaven, with Mian as Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Yichang commandery, he issued a distant edict making the crown prince commander-in-chief of all forces, with Mian as vice censor-in-chief and left guardian of the heir apparent to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是時，冕為河西行軍司馬，授御史中丞，詔赴朝廷。

translations.literal: At this time Mian was campaigning marshal in Hexi; he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and ordered to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mian was still campaigning marshal in Hexi; he was appointed vice censor-in-chief and ordered to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遇太子於平涼，具陳事勢，勸之朔方，亟入靈武。

translations.literal: He met the Heir Apparent at Pingliang, fully set forth the situation, urged him toward Shuofang, and urgently had him enter Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He met the crown prince at Pingliang, explained the situation in full, and urged him to go to Shuofang and enter Lingwu without delay.

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸、崔漪等勸進曰：「主上厭勤大位，南幸蜀川，宗社神器，須有所歸，天意人事，不可固違。

translations.literal: Mian with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged advance, saying: 'The sovereign is weary of the toil of the great position and has gone south to Shu; the altars of state and the sacred regalia must have somewhere to rest; the will of Heaven and human affairs cannot be firmly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, together with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others, urged him to take the throne, saying: 'The emperor has grown weary of rule and gone south to Shu. The altars of state and the imperial regalia must have a lord; Heaven's will and the people's need cannot be defied.

sentences.zh: 若逡巡退讓，失億兆心，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: If you hesitate and yield in retreat, losing the hearts of the hundred millions, then the great affair is gone!
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and hold back, you will lose the hearts of the people—and the cause will be lost!

sentences.zh: 臣等猶知之，況賢智乎！」

translations.literal: We your servants still know this—how much more the worthy and wise!
translations.idiomatic: Even we understand this—how much more those who are wise!

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「南平寇逆，奉迎鑾輿，退居儲貳，侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent said: 'To pacify the south of the bandits and rebels, welcome the imperial carriage, withdraw to dwell as heir designate, and attend meals at the left and right—would this not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied: 'To crush the rebels in the south, welcome the emperor home, and remain heir apparent at his side—would that not be happiness enough?

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過也？」

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen speak so excessively?'
translations.idiomatic: Why do you speak so extravagantly?

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸又進曰：「殿下藉累聖之資，有天下之表。

translations.literal: Mian and Du Hongjian again advanced, saying: 'Your Highness relies on the resources of successive sages and has the bearing to possess all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Du Hongjian pressed again: 'Your Highness inherits the virtue of generations of sage rulers and bears the countenance of one destined to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖，正在今日。

translations.literal: Your primordial constancy reaches the ten thousand states; for more than twenty years deep sorrow has opened the sage—today is exactly the time.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years your steadfast virtue has sustained the realm; it is through deep trial that the sage is revealed—and that moment is today.

sentences.zh: 所從殿下六軍將士，皆關輔百姓，日夜思歸。

translations.literal: The six-army officers and soldiers who follow Your Highness are all common people of Guanfu; day and night they think of returning.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of your six armies are all men from the Guanzhong region who long day and night to return home.

sentences.zh: 大軍一散，不可復集，不如因而撫之以從眾，臣等敢以死請。」

translations.literal: Once the great army disperses it cannot be gathered again; it is better to take the occasion and comfort them to follow the multitude—we your servants dare request this with our lives.'
translations.idiomatic: Once the army scatters it cannot be reassembled. Better to win them over now and follow the will of the troops—we beg this at the cost of our lives.

sentences.zh: 凡勸進五上，乃依。

translations.literal: In all they urged advance five times before he assented.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their appeal five times before he finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，以定策功，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，倚以為政。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, for merit in settling the plan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and relied on for government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and made a chief minister in recognition of his role in the succession, and the emperor relied on him in governing.

sentences.zh: 冕性忠勤，悉心奉公，稍得人心。

translations.literal: Mian's nature was loyal and diligent; he devoted his heart to serving the public and gradually won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was loyal and diligent, devoted himself wholly to public service, and gradually won people's confidence.

sentences.zh: 然不識大體，以聚人曰財，乃下令賣官鬻爵，度尼僧道士，以儲積為務。

translations.literal: Yet he did not understand the great substance; taking gathering people to mean wealth, he then ordered the sale of offices and ranks, ordination of Buddhist and Daoist clergy, and made accumulation his task.
translations.idiomatic: But he lacked a grasp of larger policy. Believing that amassing people was the same as amassing wealth, he ordered the sale of offices and ranks, the licensing of Buddhist and Daoist ordinations, and made hoarding revenue his chief aim.

sentences.zh: 人不願者，科令就之，其價益賤，事轉為弊。

translations.literal: Those who did not wish it were compelled by statute to comply; the prices grew ever cheaper and the affair turned into abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resisted were forced by decree to comply anyway. Prices kept falling, and the practice became a growing abuse.

sentences.zh: 肅宗移幸鳳翔，罷冕知政事，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: When Suzong moved his residence to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from managing state affairs and transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong moved the court to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from office as chief minister and made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，以功封冀國公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with an income of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋加御史大夫、成都尹，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Chengdu, serving as Military Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief and prefect of Chengdu, and appointed military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 又入為右僕射。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to serve again as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴遵慶等並集賢待制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he and Pei Zunqing and others were all made Attendants on Duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 (765) he and Pei Zunqing and others were appointed scholars on call at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 代宗求舊，拜冕兼御史大夫，充護山陵使。

translations.literal: Daizong sought old ministers and appointed Mian concurrently Censor-in-Chief, serving as Commissioner for Guarding the Imperial Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong, seeking veteran ministers, appointed Mian censor-in-chief and commissioner for guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 冕以幸臣李輔國權盛，將附之，乃表輔國親昵術士中書舍人劉烜充山陵使判官。

translations.literal: Mian, because favored minister Li Fuguo's power was flourishing and wishing to attach himself to him, memorialized that Fuguo's intimate technician, Drafting Attendant Liu Xuan, should serve as administrative aide to the tomb commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to curry favor with the powerful favorite Li Fuguo, Mian recommended Fuguo's close associate, the drafting attendant and technician Liu Xuan, as administrative aide on the tomb commission.

sentences.zh: 烜坐法，冕坐貶施州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan was guilty by law; Mian was implicated and demoted to Prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuan was convicted, Mian was implicated and demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 數月，移澧州刺史，復征為左僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was moved to Prefect of Li and again summoned as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was transferred to prefect of Li, then recalled to serve as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai held government.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai was then in control of the government.

sentences.zh: 載為新平縣尉，王鉷辟在巡內，冕常引之，載頗德冕。

translations.literal: Zai had been Magistrate of Xinping; Wang Hong recruited him within his circuit inspection, and Mian often recommended him—Zai was quite grateful to Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once been magistrate of Xinping. When Wang Hong recruited him into his inspection staff, Mian had often spoken well of him, and Zai felt deep gratitude toward Mian.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣杜鴻漸卒，載遂舉冕代之。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Du Hongjian died, Zai then recommended Mian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Du Hongjian died, Zai recommended Mian to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 冕時已衰瘵，載以其順己，引為同列。

translations.literal: Mian was already declining with illness; Zai, because he complied with him, drew him in as a fellow minister.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was by then aged and ill, but Zai, knowing he would not oppose him, brought him into the chief ministry as a colleague.

sentences.zh: 受命之際，蹈舞絕倒，載趨而扶起，代為謝詞。

translations.literal: At the moment of receiving the appointment he danced and collapsed in a faint; Zai hurried to support him and spoke thanks on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the appointment he performed the ritual dance and collapsed in a faint. Zai rushed forward to support him and delivered the words of thanks on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 冕兼掌兵權留守之任，俸錢每月二千余貫。

translations.literal: Mian concurrently held military authority and the duty of regent; his salary cash was more than two thousand strings per month.
translations.idiomatic: Mian also held military authority and the post of regent, with a monthly salary of more than two thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 性本侈靡，好尚車服及營珍饌，名馬在櫪，直數百金者常十數。

translations.literal: His nature was by origin extravagant; he loved carriages and robes and preparing rare delicacies; famous horses in the stable worth several hundred gold pieces numbered a dozen or so regularly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant, fond of fine carriages and robes and of preparing rare delicacies. He kept a dozen or more famous horses in his stables, each worth several hundred gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 每會賓友，滋味品數，坐客有昧於名者。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered guests and friends, the flavors and varieties were such that seated guests were ignorant of the names.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entertained guests, the dishes were so numerous and exotic that those seated at table could not even name them all.

sentences.zh: 自創巾子，其狀新奇，市肆因而效之，呼為「僕射樣」。

translations.literal: He himself created a headcloth; its form was novel, and market shops therefore imitated it, calling it the 'Vice Director style.'
translations.idiomatic: He designed a new style of official headcloth so striking in form that shops across the city copied it, calling it the 'vice director style.'

sentences.zh: 初代鴻漸，小吏以俸錢文簿白之，冕顧子弟，喜見於色，其嗜利若此。

translations.literal: When he first replaced Hongjian, a petty clerk reported the salary accounts to him; Mian looked at his sons and younger brothers, delight showing in his expression—his craving for profit was like this.
translations.idiomatic: When he first succeeded Du Hongjian, a clerk presented the salary ledger. Mian turned to his sons and brothers with unmistakable delight on his face—such was his love of gain.

sentences.zh: 拜職未盈月，卒，大歷四年十二月也。

translations.literal: He had not completed a full month in the appointment when he died—in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He had held office less than a month when he died, in the twelfth month of Dali 4 (769).

sentences.zh: 上悼之，輟朝三日，贈太尉，賻制五百匹、粟五百石。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal, and granted funeral gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned his death, suspended court for three days, posthumously made him grand marshal, and granted five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing was a man of Wenxi in Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing was a native of Wenxi in Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代襲冠冕，為河東著族。

translations.literal: For generations they inherited caps and coronets and were a distinguished clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held high office for generations and ranked among the leading clans of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵慶志氣深厚，機鑒敏達，自幼強學，博涉載籍，謹身晦跡，不幹當世之務。

translations.literal: Zunqing's will and spirit were deep and thick, his insight keen and penetrating; from youth he studied strenuously, broadly traversed written records, kept himself cautious and hid his traces, and did not meddle in the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was deep-spirited and keen-witted. From childhood he studied hard and read widely, yet he kept a low profile and did not thrust himself into public affairs.

sentences.zh: 以門廕累授潞府司法參軍，時年已老，未為人所知。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was repeatedly appointed Legal Administrator of the Lu prefecture office; at the time he was already old and not yet known to people.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose to legal administrator in the Lu prefecture office, but he was already advanced in years and still little known.

sentences.zh: 隨調吏部，授大理寺丞，剖斷刑獄，舉正綱條，理行始著。

translations.literal: Following transfer at the Ministry of Personnel, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; in deciding criminal cases he upheld the statutes and regulations, and his governing conduct first became notable.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the regular transfer process at the Ministry of Personnel, he was appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review. In judging criminal cases he upheld the law firmly, and his reputation for good governance began to spread.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外、吏部員外郎，專判南曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Gate Office and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, exclusively deciding the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Gate Office and vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, with sole charge of the southern bureau of selection.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，海內無事，九流輻輳會府，每歲吏部選人，動盈萬數。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the realm within the seas was without affairs; the nine currents converged like wheel spokes at the capital offices, and each year Ministry of Personnel candidates commonly exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era the empire was at peace, and candidates of every sort thronged the capital. Each year those presenting themselves for selection at the Ministry of Personnel routinely numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敏識強記，精核文簿，詳而不滯，時稱吏事第一，由是大知名。

translations.literal: Zunqing was keen in perception and strong in memory; he examined documents minutely, was detailed yet not obstructed, and at the time was called first in clerical affairs—thereby he became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was quick-witted and possessed a formidable memory. He scrutinized documents with precision, thorough yet never bogged down, and was acclaimed the foremost man of administrative affairs—winning wide fame.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠當國，出不附己者例為外官，遵慶亦出為郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Yang Guozhong held the state; those who did not attach to him were by rule made outer officials, and Zunqing too was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao era Yang Guozhong dominated the government and routinely posted opponents to provincial office. Zunqing too was sent out as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，征拜給事中、尚書右丞、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting attendant, right assistant in the Secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 恭儉克己，遲重謹密，頗有時望。

translations.literal: Respectful and frugal, he restrained himself; slow, weighty, cautious and discreet—he had considerable contemporary esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful, frugal, and self-restrained, grave and discreet in manner, and enjoyed considerable standing at court.

sentences.zh: 上元中，蕭華輔政，素知遵慶，每奏見，累稱之，遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era Xiao Hua assisted in government, had long known Zunqing, and whenever he memorialized at audience repeatedly praised him; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Gate and Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era Xiao Hua, who had long known Zunqing's worth, repeatedly praised him at audience. Zunqing was promoted to vice director of the palace gate and made a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，仆固懷恩阻兵汾上，指中官為詞，上以遵慶忠純，特遣往汾州宣慰懷恩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde Pugu Huai'en blocked troops on the Fen; he pointed to inner eunuchs as his pretext; the emperor, because Zunqing was loyal and pure, specially sent him to Fen prefecture to proclaim consolation to Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era Pugu Huai'en held his army on the Fen River and made the eunuchs his excuse for defiance. The emperor, trusting Zunqing's loyalty, specially dispatched him to Fen prefecture to reassure Huai'en on the court's behalf.

sentences.zh: 遵慶既見懷恩，具陳朝旨，懷恩引過聽命，將隨遵慶朝謁，為副將範誌誠以邪說惑之，懷恩遂以懼死為詞。

translations.literal: After Zunqing met Huai'en he fully set forth the court's intent; Huai'en acknowledged his fault and obeyed orders, and was about to follow Zunqing to court audience, but was deluded by his deputy general Fan Zhicheng with perverse talk—Huai'en then used fear of death as his plea.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing met Huai'en he explained the court's position in full. Huai'en admitted his error and agreed to obey, and was preparing to accompany Zunqing to court—but his deputy Fan Zhicheng turned him with seditious counsel, and Huai'en then pleaded that he feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 會蕃寇陷京師，乘輿幸陜，遵慶自汾州奔赴行在。

translations.literal: When Tibetan bandits seized the capital and the imperial carriage went to Shan, Zunqing from Fen prefecture rushed to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan forces took the capital and the emperor fled to Shan, Zunqing hurried from Fen prefecture to join the court in exile.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿還京，以遵慶為太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Zunqing was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zunqing was appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴冕等並於集賢院待制，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he and Pei Mian and others were all made Attendants on Duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and ceased managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 (765) he and Pei Mian and others were appointed scholars on call at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and were removed from the chief ministry.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部尚書、右僕射，復知選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Minister of Personnel and Right Vice Director and again managed selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of personnel and right vice director and again put in charge of civil-service selection.

sentences.zh: 時選人天興縣尉陳琯於銓庭言詞不遜，淩突無禮，代宗詔付遵慶於省門鞭三十，貶為吉州員外司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At the time the candidate Chen Guan, Magistrate of Tianxing, used insubordinate words in the selection courtyard, arrogant and without propriety; Daizong ordered him handed to Zunqing for thirty lashes at the ministry gate and demoted to Outside Registrar of Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When a candidate named Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing, spoke insolently and behaved outrageously at the selection bureau, Emperor Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty times at the ministry gate and demoted him to outside registrar of Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敦守儒行，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: Zunqing earnestly kept Confucian conduct and in old age became all the more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing steadfastly upheld Confucian conduct and grew only more careful in his old age.

sentences.zh: 嘗為風狂族侄撾登聞鼓告以不順，上知遵度，不省，其見信如此。

translations.literal: Once a mad cousin by the clan beat the Denunciation Drum at the Gate of Imperial Audience and reported him for disloyalty; the emperor knew Zunqing and did not investigate—such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a deranged kinsman beat the Denunciation Drum at the Gate of Imperial Audience and accused him of disloyalty. The emperor, knowing Zunqing's character, paid no heed—such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年十月薨於位，年九十余。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Dali he died in office at more than ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Dali 10 (775) he died in office at more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 遵慶初登省郎，嘗著《王政記》，述今古禮體，識者覽之，知有公輔之量。

translations.literal: When Zunqing first entered as a provincial bureau gentleman he once authored 'Record of Royal Government,' setting forth ancient and modern ritual forms; those of discernment who read it knew he had the capacity of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career as a capital bureau officer he wrote Record of Royal Government, treating ritual institutions past and present. Readers of discernment recognized in it the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 子向，字傃仁，少以門廕歷官至太子司議郎。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, courtesy name Siren, from youth through hereditary privilege rose in office to Senior Remonstrator of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, courtesy name Siren, entered office through hereditary privilege and rose to senior remonstrator of the heir apparent while still young.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏向為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Li Shu was Prefect of Tong prefecture and memorialized Xiang as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era Li Shu, as prefect of Tong, recommended Xiang as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong and sent his general Zhao Guixian to build ramparts at Tong prefecture; Shu came fleeing to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled and Li Huai'guang rose in Hezhong, Huai'guang sent his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong. Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang was left in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貴先因脅縣尉林寶役徒板築，不及期，將斬之，吏人百姓奔竄。

translations.literal: Guixian compelled the county magistrate Lin Bao to press laborers for plank construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead him, and clerks, people, and commoners fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian forced the county magistrate Lin Bao to press the laborers in building the ramparts. When the work fell behind schedule he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 向即詣貴先軍壘，以逆順之理責之，貴先感悟，遂來降，故同州不陷。

translations.literal: Xiang immediately went to Guixian's army ramparts and reproached him with the principle of rebellion and obedience; Guixian was moved to understanding and then came to surrender—therefore Tong prefecture did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went at once to Guixian's camp and rebuked him on the grounds of loyalty and rebellion. Guixian was moved to repentance and surrendered, and so Tong prefecture was saved.

sentences.zh: 向由是知名。

translations.literal: From this Xiang became known.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Xiang's name became known.

sentences.zh: 累為京兆府戶曹，轉櫟陽、渭南縣令，奏課皆第一，朝廷亟聞其理行，擢為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as Revenue Clerk of the Metropolitan Prefecture, was transferred to Magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; his memorial evaluations were all first, the court quickly heard of his governing conduct, and he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the metropolitan revenue office and then as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan, earning top ratings in every evaluation. The court soon took note of his governance and promoted him to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗季年，天下方鎮副亻卒多自選於朝，防一日有變，遂就而授之節制。

translations.literal: In Dezong's late years, deputy commanders of the realm's regional commands were mostly selected from the court themselves, guarding against sudden change one day—thereupon they were granted military commission on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Dezong's reign, deputy commanders for the regional armies were often chosen in advance at court, so that if trouble arose they could immediately be given full military commission.

sentences.zh: 向已選為太原少尹，德宗召見喻旨，尋用為行軍司馬、兼御史中丞，改汾州刺史，轉鄭州。

translations.literal: Xiang had already been selected as Junior Prefect of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him for audience and explained the intent; soon he was employed as campaigning marshal and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, changed to Prefect of Fen, and transferred to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had been selected as junior prefect of Taiyuan. Emperor Dezong summoned him, explained his intentions, and soon appointed him campaigning marshal and vice censor-in-chief, then prefect of Fen and later of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 又復為太原少尹，兼河東節度副使。

translations.literal: He again became Junior Prefect of Taiyuan and concurrently Deputy Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made junior prefect of Taiyuan and deputy military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 改晉州刺史，充本州防禦使，遷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Jin, served as Defense Commissioner of that prefecture, and was transferred to Prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jin and defense commissioner there, then transferred to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆少尹，拜同州刺史，充本州防禦使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Prefect of the Metropolitan Prefecture, was appointed Prefect of Tong, and served as Defense Commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as junior metropolitan prefect, appointed prefect of Tong, and made defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為大理寺卿，出遷陜虢都防禦、觀察使。

translations.literal: He entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, went out and was transferred to Defense and Investigation Commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Court of Judicial Review, then sent out as defense and investigation commissioner for Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 三歲，拜左散騎常侍，自常侍復為大理。

translations.literal: After three years he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and from Regular Attendant returned to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was made left regular attendant of the cavalry, then returned from that post to serve again as director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 向本以名相子，以學行自飭，謹守其門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was originally the son of a famous chief minister; by learning and conduct he restrained himself and carefully kept his family's style.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was born the son of a famous chief minister and disciplined himself through learning and conduct, carefully preserving his family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 歷官仁智推愛，利及於人。

translations.literal: Through his offices he extended benevolence and wisdom with love, and benefit reached people.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he governed with benevolence and wisdom, bringing benefit to those under him.

sentences.zh: 至是，以年過致政，朝廷優異，乃以吏部尚書致仕於新昌裏第。

translations.literal: At this point, because his years had passed he retired from government; the court treated him with exceptional favor and he retired as Minister of Personnel at his residence in Xinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old he retired from office. The court treated him with exceptional honor, allowing him to retire with the title of minister of personnel at his home in Xinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 內外支屬百余人，向所得俸祿，必同其費，及領外任，亦挈而隨之。

translations.literal: Inner and outer branch relatives numbered more than a hundred; whatever salary Xiang received he always shared the expenses, and when he took outer posts he also brought them along.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred kinsmen, close and distant, depended on him. Whatever salary he received he shared with them all, and when he took provincial office he brought them with him.

sentences.zh: 有孤煢疾苦不能自恤，向尤周給，至今稱其孝睦焉。

translations.literal: There were orphans and the solitary, the ill and suffering who could not care for themselves—Xiang especially provided for them roundly; to this day they praise his filiality and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the destitute, and the sick who could not care for themselves he especially supported. To this day he is praised for his filial devotion and kindness to kin.

sentences.zh: 大和四年九月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Dahe he died at eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Dahe 4 (830) at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子寅，登進士第，累官至御史大夫卒。

translations.literal: His son Yin passed the jinshi examination and through repeated offices reached Censor-in-Chief before dying.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin passed the jinshi examination and rose through several posts to censor-in-chief, in which office he died.

sentences.zh: 子樞，字紀聖，咸通十二年登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Shu, courtesy name Jisheng, in the twelfth year of Xiantong passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu, courtesy name Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination in Xiantong 12 (871).

sentences.zh: 宰相杜審權出鎮河中，辟為從事，得秘書省校書郎，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Du Shenquan went out to garrison Hezhong and recruited him as administrative aide; he obtained Collator in the Secretariat and was twice transferred to Magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong, he recruited Shu as administrative aide. Shu was appointed collator in the Secretariat and later promoted twice to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館。

translations.literal: He served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo deeply knew him; when Duo was removed from the chief ministry and lost his post, Shu also for a long time received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him. When Duo lost the chief ministry and fell from power, Shu too went long without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，中丞李煥奏為殿中侍御史，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He followed Xizong to Shu; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Huan memorialized him as Attending Censor in the Palace, and he was transferred to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Xizong to Shu. Vice censor-in-chief Li Huan recommended him as attending censor in the palace, and he was promoted to diarist.

sentences.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe Wang Duo was again employed; because of old grace he was transferred to Secretary of Zheng and Hua, Investigating Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, granted gold and purple, entered court and passed through Vice Director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe era Wang Duo returned to power. Out of old friendship Shu was made secretary to the Zheng-Hua command and investigating director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, granted the gold-and-purple insignia, and after returning to court served as vice director in the ministries of War and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，擢拜給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was promoted and appointed Drafting Attendant, then changed to Metropolitan Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longji era he was promoted to drafting attendant and then made metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯尤深獎遇。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Kong Wei especially deeply rewarded and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Kong Wei especially favored and promoted him.

sentences.zh: 大順中，緯以用兵無功貶官，樞坐累為右庶子，尋出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: In Dazhun Wei was demoted for using troops without merit; Shu was implicated and made Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhun era Kong Wei was demoted for military failure. Shu was implicated and made right guardian of the heir apparent, then sent out as prefect of She.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, followed Zhaozong to Hua prefecture, and served as Proclamation and Consolation Commissioner to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianning era he was recalled as right regular attendant of the cavalry, accompanied Emperor Zhaozong to Hua, and was appointed commissioner to proclaim the court's will at Bian.

sentences.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shu from She prefecture left his command and returned to court, his route passed through Daliang; at the time Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising; Shu treated him as an elder brother, and Quanzhong therefore valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shu left his post at She and returned to court, his route took him through Daliang. Zhu Quanzhong's military power was already formidable, and Shu treated him with the deference due an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shu transmitted the edict, Quanzhong all followed court intent; tribute and offerings followed in succession; Zhaozong was very pleased and transferred him to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu delivered the imperial edict, Quanzhong obeyed the court's every instruction and sent tribute in unbroken succession. Emperor Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized government and also relied on Quanzhong; the two therefore joined together and changed Shu to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was then dominant at court and also relied on Quanzhong. The two formed an alliance, and Shu was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，換戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was exchanged to Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to vice minister of revenue and appointed a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Hua prefecture; Cui Yin was demoted, and Shu also became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Zhaozong went to Hua. When Cui Yin was demoted, Shu was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Investigating Right Vice Director and Concurrent Regular Attendant, and sent out as Military Commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital from Qi, Shu was made investigating right vice director and chief minister, then sent out as military commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, Zhu Quanzhong recommended and protected him, saying Shu had talent to order the age and could not be abandoned to the southern ranges; soon he was again appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, repeatedly held concurrently Minister of Personnel, and decided revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, Zhu Quanzhong intervened on his behalf, declaring that Shu possessed talent to govern the realm and should not be banished to the far south. Shu was soon made vice director of the Chancellery, put in charge of compiling the national history, and eventually also minister of personnel with charge of revenue.

sentences.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because Quanzhong had long been close his chief-minister position remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Yin was executed, Shu retained his chief ministry unchanged, thanks to his long-standing ties with Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He followed Zhaozong in moving to Luoyang, halted at Shan prefecture, was advanced to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, and served as Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Zhaozong to Luoyang and, when the court halted at Shan, was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, and transport commissioner for salt and iron across all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？

translations.literal: When Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized to employ his military officer Zhang Tingfan as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chief ministers discussed it, and Shu said: 'Tingfan is a meritorious minister—fortunately he may receive a regional command with military commission; what need has he of the Director of Music?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi first took the throne, Liu Can was in power. Quanzhong once recommended his military officer Zhang Tingfan as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The chief ministers deliberated, and Shu said, 'Tingfan is a meritorious officer who may yet receive a regional command—why does he need the directorship of the Court of Sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 恐非元帥梁王之旨。」

translations.literal: I fear this is not the intent of the Marshal, King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not what the Prince of Liang, our commander-in-chief, intends.

sentences.zh: 乃持之不下。

translations.literal: He therefore held it and did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore withheld the appointment and would not issue it.

sentences.zh: 俄而全忠聞樞言，謂賓佐曰：「吾常以裴十四器識真純，不入浮薄之伍，觀此議論，本態露矣。」

translations.literal: Soon Quanzhong heard Shu's words and said to his guests and aides: 'I always considered Pei the Fourteenth's capacity and insight truly pure, not entering the ranks of the frivolous and shallow—viewing this discussion, his true nature is revealed.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong heard of Shu's words he told his staff, 'I always thought Pei the Fourteenth was genuinely upright and would never join the frivolous crowd—but this opinion shows his true colors.

sentences.zh: 切齒含怒。

translations.literal: He gnashed his teeth and harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: He ground his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to suit the intent, removed Shu from the chief-minister position; at the joint offering at He Mausoleum he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, hearing Quanzhong's anger, soon had Shu removed from the chief ministry in accord with his wishes. At the joint offering at He Mausoleum Shu was made left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，責授朝散大夫、登州刺史，尋再貶瀧州司戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was punished and appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Prefect of Deng, soon again demoted to Registrar of Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was demoted to grand master of palace leisure and prefect of Deng, then soon further demoted to registrar of Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月十一日，行及滑州，全忠遣人殺之於白馬驛，投屍於河，時年六十五。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when his journey reached Hua prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post, threw the corpse into the river—he was sixty-five years of age.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when he reached Hua prefecture on his way into exile, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post and throw his body into the river. He was sixty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉卿謹身蒞事，足為純臣，避寇全忠，固彰大節。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Jingqing kept himself cautious in attending to affairs—sufficient to be a pure minister; avoiding bandits he preserved complete loyalty, truly displaying great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments: Jingqing conducted himself with scrupulous care in office and may truly be called a loyal minister; in fleeing the rebels he preserved his integrity and displayed great moral courage.
