sentences.zh: 然博達精審，豈不知寬猛之道哉！

translations.literal: Yet broad, penetrating, and precise in examination—how could he not know the way of leniency and severity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was learned, penetrating, and exact in judgment—how could he not have known the balance of leniency and severity!

sentences.zh: 奉林甫之旨，順胥吏之意，悅附張倚，欺罔時君。

translations.literal: He followed Linfu's intent, complied with the clerks' wishes, delighted in attaching to Zhang Yi, and deceived and misled the ruler of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out Li Linfu's wishes, indulged the clerks, curried favor with Zhang Yi, and deceived his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 生為重臣，諂林甫之勢也；

translations.literal: While alive he was a great minister—this was fawning on Linfu's power;
translations.idiomatic: In life he rose to the highest office by flattering Li Linfu's power;

sentences.zh: 歿改美謚，引元載之恩焉。

translations.literal: after death he received a fine posthumous title—this drew on Yuan Zai's grace.
translations.idiomatic: after death he received a flattering posthumous title through Yuan Zai's favor.

sentences.zh: 或言晉卿不為巧宦者，誠不信也。

translations.literal: If some say Jingqing was not a crafty official, truly one cannot believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who claim Jingqing was no crafty courtier simply cannot be believed.

sentences.zh: 冕力贊中興，名居大位，奉公抱義，可以致身；

translations.literal: Mian vigorously praised the restoration, his name occupied the great position, he served the public and embraced righteousness—by this one could establish oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Mian vigorously supported the restoration and rose to the highest rank. In serving the state with integrity he might have won lasting honor;

sentences.zh: 賣官度僧，是何為政？

translations.literal: selling offices and licensing monks—what kind of government is this?
translations.idiomatic: yet what sort of governance is it to sell offices and sell ordinations?

sentences.zh: 及其老也，貪冒尤深。

translations.literal: When he reached old age, his greed and presumption were especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age his greed knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 遵慶學術貞明，為國忠所出；

translations.literal: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear, yet he was sent out by Guozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing's learning was upright and his conduct clear, yet Yang Guozhong had him posted to the provinces;

sentences.zh: 恭儉謹密，遇蕭華素知。

translations.literal: respectful, frugal, cautious and discreet—he met Xiao Hua, who had long known him.
translations.idiomatic: he was respectful, frugal, and discreet, and won recognition from Xiao Hua, who had long known his worth.

sentences.zh: 位重行純，老而彌篤，彼二公固有慚德。

translations.literal: His position was weighty and his conduct pure; in old age he became all the more earnest—those two lords naturally had conduct to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: He held high office with pure conduct and grew only more steadfast in old age—beside him, the other two men had reason to feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 向克荷堂構，不墜門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was able to bear the hall's beams and did not let the family's style fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld the family estate and did not let its reputation fall.

sentences.zh: 樞因盜而振，盜憎而亡，宜哉！

translations.literal: Shu rose through the bandit, the bandit hated him and he perished—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose through the rebel's favor, and when the rebel turned against him he perished—as was only fitting!

sentences.zh: 君子守道遠刑，蓋慮此也。

translations.literal: The gentleman keeps the Way and stays far from punishment—probably he considers this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman holds to the Way and keeps clear of punishment—surely he takes warning from such examples.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：奧矣晉卿，貪哉裴冕。

translations.literal: The praise says: profound is Jingqing, greedy is Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Jingqing was deep in cunning; Pei Mian was deep in greed.

sentences.zh: 遵慶父子，及之者鮮。

translations.literal: Zunqing, father and sons—few reach them.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zunqing and his sons, few could equal them.
